subject: Multiple group analysis with covariance matrices input

messages.author: 7d2f2f454e708927
messages.subject: Multiple group analysis with covariance matrices input
parts:
Hi, all.

I have tried to conduct a simply multiple group analysis with only one variable with the summary statistics as input. It gives an error message. Any suggestions? Thanks.

lower <- '11.834'
my.df1 <- getCov(lower, diag=TRUE, names=c("x"))
lower <- '12.834'
my.df2 <- getCov(lower, diag=TRUE, names=c("x"))
Cov <- list(my.df1, my.df2)

Mean <- list(10, 12)
N <- c(250, 220)

model <- 'x~~x
          x~1'

fit <- sem(model, sample.cov=Cov, sample.mean=Mean, sample.nobs=N, meanstructure=TRUE)

Error in row(S) : a matrix-like object is required as argument to 'row'

Regards,
Nowell

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multiple group analysis with covariance matrices input
parts:
I ran into the same error message once when I tried fitting an ANOVA as an SEM, using FIML for missing data (i.e., using raw data rather than supplying sample moments).  I don't think your error has anything to do with how you are supplying data to lavaan.  I think it happens somewhere the data is manipulated internally, but I never tracked down exactly where.  The syntax "row(S" only appears in the lavaan source code in the vech() function in the file lav_matrix.R (line 34), but that function is called in 83 locations in the lavaan source files.  Yves would have a better idea where to look, and he might be able to put in a check for variables that only have a single observed variable, coercing the variance to be a matrix instead of a length-1 vector.  It's probably so rare that it hasn't been reported before -- I just got around the problem by adding another outcome (MANOVA) so there would be more elements in the covariance matrix.

Terry
